title: The rent won't cover the instalment by RM600 a month. Should I still buy?
excerpt: A Malaysian working in New Zealand is weighing a resale unit near an MRT station that needs a RM500 to RM600 monthly top-up, and family tips on gold. Sean says move on and look further.

question.asker: From K, a viewer who wrote in by email
question.context: K works in New Zealand, where mortgage rates are 7% to 8%, and takes home about RM12,000 a month. A condo in Taman Desa is rented out and covers its repayment, and K plans to settle its remaining RM69,000 loan within months. K is considering a resale unit of about RM467,000 near an MRT station in Kuala Lumpur, with a 10% rebate, but nearby rents suggest a RM500 to RM600 monthly top-up. Family members say gold is the better buy right now.
question.text: Should K buy gold instead, take the resale unit, or look at high-density projects around Sunway Velocity?

answer.quote: Why must you settle for a project that cannot make money?
answer.summary: Don't commit to a unit you already know will cost you RM500 to RM600 a month; keep looking until you find one where the rent covers the instalment. As for gold, check whether the people recommending it have the results you want, and invest in what you understand.

reasons.title: Judge the advice by the adviser
reasons.body: Tips from relatives are often second-hand, from a short video or a sales commission. Sean puts his money in property because he knows it well, and sees the asset you understand best as the safest one.

reasons.title: There are always other projects
reasons.body: Buyers often fix on one development, then blame the developer or the market when it doesn't pay. Sean says view 20 projects of different types, ages and areas and move on from any that can't make money.

reasons.title: Developers sell at the recommended retail price
reasons.body: Investors try to buy below it: through subsale, where the owner's urgency gives room to negotiate; auctions, which can carry caveats, title problems or unpaid maintenance; or bulk purchase deals.

reasons.title: Settling a covered loan may waste cash
reasons.body: The Taman Desa rent already covers its instalment, so paying off the last RM69,000 may not be the best use of the money; it could fund another unit where the rent covers the loan. Sean couldn't judge this fully without knowing K's age.

actions: Ask whoever recommends gold or any other investment whether they have invested in it themselves and got the results you want.
Drop any unit whose rent won't cover the instalment, however close it is to a station.
View around 20 projects of different types and locations before choosing.
Compare subsale, auction and bulk purchase prices against the developer's price.
Before settling a loan the rent already covers, compare that with using the cash as a down payment elsewhere.
caveat: Sean sees no legal problem with a unit resold after the first buyer's SPA was cancelled. Auctions are harder to manage from overseas, so he wouldn't suggest them for K.
sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #233. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as the viewer stated them in December 2023; rates vary between countries and over time.
